frameworks.label: Frameworks
frameworks.meta: Q: WHICH ML FRAMEWORKS ARE IN PRODUCTION USE?

rows.label: PyTorch
rows.note: Now the default training stack for the majority of respondents, including teams that previously reported TensorFlow.

rows.label: scikit-learn
rows.note: Still the most common library for tabular production workloads despite the shift toward deep learning.

rows.label: TensorFlow
rows.note: Continued decline, largely in teams migrating existing serving pipelines rather than new projects.

rows.label: XGBoost / LightGBM
rows.note: Stable: gradient boosting remains dominant for risk, fraud and forecasting use cases.

rows.label: ONNX runtime
rows.note: Growing with edge and cross-vendor deployment, aligned to the cross-vendor GPU computing work.

rows.label: JAX
rows.note: Concentrated in research-heavy organisations and frontier-model teams.

challenges.label: Production challenges
challenges.meta: Q: TOP CHALLENGES TAKING MODELS TO PRODUCTION

rows.label: Monitoring & drift
rows.note: Maps to Principle 04 — reproducible operations — and the observability failures in the MLSecOps Top 10.

rows.label: Data quality
rows.note: Persistently the first-order problem; feeds directly into bias evaluation under Principle 02.

rows.label: Deployment complexity
rows.note: Easing slightly as orchestration tooling matures, but still a top-three blocker.

rows.label: Security & data risk
rows.note: The fastest-rising challenge, and the reason the MLSecOps Top 10 exists.

rows.label: Reproducibility
rows.note: Improving where experiment tracking and lineage are adopted as infrastructure, not convention.

rows.label: Explainability
rows.note: Rising with regulatory pressure; addressed by the XAI Framework’s three-stage model.

cloud.label: Platforms
cloud.meta: Q: WHERE ARE PRODUCTION WORKLOADS RUNNING?

rows.label: AWS
rows.note: Remains the plurality choice for production ML infrastructure.

rows.label: Microsoft Azure
rows.note: Growth concentrated in regulated industries and enterprises with existing Microsoft estates.

rows.label: Google Cloud
rows.note: Stable share, with strength in data-platform-led organisations.

rows.label: On-premise / private
rows.note: Rising with data-residency requirements and GPU cost control.

rows.label: Hybrid across vendors
rows.note: The case for cross-vendor GPU computing and portable runtimes such as Kompute.

rows.label: MLflow
rows.note: Still the open-source default, frequently self-hosted alongside internal tooling.

rows.label: Weights & Biases
rows.note: Strongest in deep-learning and research-adjacent teams.

rows.label: Internal tooling
rows.note: Declining as managed and open-source options mature.

rows.label: No formal tracking
rows.note: Falling, but one in five teams still cannot reproduce a production model’s training run.

rows.label: Neptune / Comet / other
rows.note: A long tail of specialist tools, often chosen for compliance reporting.

genai.label: Generative AI
genai.meta: Q: WHICH GENERATIVE-AI PROVIDERS ARE IN USE?

rows.label: OpenAI
rows.note: Most widely integrated provider, typically through hosted APIs rather than fine-tuning.

rows.label: Anthropic
rows.note: The largest year-on-year increase in the survey.

rows.label: Open-weight models
rows.note: Driven by data-residency, cost control and the ability to evaluate models directly.

rows.label: Azure OpenAI
rows.note: Preferred where enterprise procurement and compliance sit with Microsoft.

rows.label: Google
rows.note: Concentrated in organisations already standardised on Google Cloud.

governance.label: Governance
governance.meta: Q: WHICH RESPONSIBLE-AI PRACTICES ARE FORMALISED?

rows.label: Documented model review
rows.note: The most common first step, usually a sign-off gate before production release.

rows.label: Bias evaluation process
rows.note: Principle 02 in practice — still absent in three-quarters of organisations.

rows.label: Human-in-the-loop policy
rows.note: Principle 01: mandatory review where the consequence of an incorrect prediction is high.

rows.label: ML security programme
rows.note: Nearly doubled year on year, tracking the rise of agentic deployments.

rows.label: Procurement assessment
rows.note: Where AI-RFX and the Machine Learning Maturity Model are applied directly.
